name: Vasculitis

criteria.description: Histopathologic evidence of blood vessel inflammation
Presence of clinical signs consistent with vasculitis such as palpable purpura or mononeuritis multiplex
Angiographic or radiologic evidence of vessel stenosis, aneurysm, or occlusion
Presence of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) or other relevant serologic markers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic evidence of vasculitis plus compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, laboratory, imaging, and histopathologic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Non-blanching raised purpuric lesions typical of small vessel vasculitis
Asymmetric peripheral nerve involvement due to vessel inflammation

searchTerms: general symptoms like fever and weight loss
feeling unwell with fever and tiredness

common.notes: Joint pain or inflammation without erosions

common.symptomName: Renal impairment with hematuria or proteinuria
searchTerms: kidney problems with blood or protein in urine
impaired kidney function with urinary abnormalities
renal damage causing hematuria or proteinuria

common.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms including cough and hemoptysis
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms including blood in sputum
eye inflammation like uveitis or scleritis
stomach pain from poor blood flow

occasional.notes: Secondary to vascular leakage or renal dysfunction
Due to involvement of cerebral vessels or nerves
searchTerms: headaches and nerve problems in head
pain and nerve issues in the head

rare.symptomName: Cardiac involvement including myocarditis or pericarditis

searchTerms: hormone problems caused by blood vessel inflammation
gland dysfunction due to vessel disease

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as depression or cognitive impairment
rare.notes: Secondary to CNS vasculitis or systemic illness
searchTerms: mental health issues like low mood or thinking difficulties

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in renal involvement
imaging: Angiography showing vessel stenosis, aneurysms, or occlusions
Chest X-ray or CT showing pulmonary infiltrates or hemorrhage
MRI or CT for CNS vasculitis evaluation
genetic: No specific genetic markers; some HLA associations reported in subsets
other: Histopathologic confirmation via biopsy demonstrating vessel wall inflammation and necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Segmental vascular occlusion without systemic inflammation
Presence of ANA and other lupus-specific antibodies
Multisystem involvement with characteristic clinical features

redFlags: Mononeuritis multiplex or rapidly progressive neuropathy
